source.title: Spectral Edge Dynamics Reveal Functional Modes of Learning

record.tranche_reason: The study tests grokking on small modular-arithmetic tasks and compares weight-decay settings, but does not report the original claim's full training-versus-test accuracy trajectory or dataset-size sweep.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy above 95% within 5000 steps for four operations and states that two other operations do not grok. It does not give training-accuracy trajectories, chance-level test values, or a sweep over training-set size. Spectral-gap and Fourier results are not separate rows because they do not measure the behavioral outcomes named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Grokking on modular arithmetic is the study's setting, not its object. Operations are sorted into grokking and non-grokking groups by a >95%-within-5000-steps criterion. All reported results concern the author's spectral-edge and functional-mode analyses. The study reports no training-accuracy curves, no chance-level start, no delay, no dataset-size sweep and no explicit test accuracy for the wd=0 runs, so its own results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that spectral-edge directions during grokking are low-dimensional functional modes over the input domain rather than localized parameter or activation structures. Head attribution, activation rank and SAE analyses fail to capture them. The modes collapse to single Fourier components when the task has a matching group basis, and spread across several or compositional modes otherwise. Shared multitask training promotes their reuse. The authors restrict their claims to modular arithmetic in small transformers.
record.recipe_differences: Uses small transformers trained on modular arithmetic and reports grokking outcomes, but focuses on spectral-update geometry and functional perturbations rather than reproducing the original study's full accuracy-trajectory and training-set-size measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking and spectral-edge formation differ with weight decay: the reported grokking runs use weight decay = 1.0, while weight-decay-zero conditions serve as controls.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral-gap (g23) decline separates grokking from non-grokking runs (Table 1). All 12 grokking runs (wd=1.0, 4 ops) show a 15–110× decline (mean 40×). Only 1 of 24 control runs shows a comparable decline. The spectral edge is described as forming during memorization and sharpening at the grokking transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low-dimensional spectral edge in weight updates accompanies grokking and forms only under weight decay. This is a candidate progress-type signal, but it is a geometric measure, not a circuit or accuracy measure.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral-edge directions concentrate on Fourier frequencies matching known grokking circuits. Addition: ω≈25–26, F up to 0.40 vs uniform baseline 0.021. Multiplication: ω=29 in the discrete-log basis. Subtraction and x²+y² show no clean structure. In a shared-trunk multitask model, x²+y² shows higher additive concentration (F 0.09→0.20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fourier structure of the final grokked circuit is visible in training-update directions, and multitask training promotes reuse of functional modes.

record.problems: The behavioral results are reported at group level rather than as per-task, per-seed accuracy trajectories. The study does not provide training accuracy, chance-level test accuracy, or a training-set-size sweep for the claim's central timing and scaling assertions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: spectral-gap, Fourier-concentration, activation-rank, and SAE-overlap results do not directly measure the behavioral outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Not tested: training-accuracy saturation, test accuracy starting at chance, the length of the delay, and the delay's dependence on training-set size. Only a 50/50 split is used.

Not tested: gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, and whether a circuit-level progress measure anticipates the jump. The spectral-edge measures concern update geometry, not circuit formation.
Not tested: non-algorithmic data, initialization scale and lazy-to-rich transitions.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Not tested: efficiency comparison of circuits, critical dataset size and ungrokking. A wd=0 vs wd=1.0 contrast exists only as a control labelling, with no reported accuracies.
Not tested: no comparison of algorithms across architectures or hyperparameters. Fourier spectra are shown for seed 42 only.
Not tested: optimizer or floating-point artifacts. AdamW is used throughout.

missing.what: Grokking steps reported for the tri-task shared-trunk model (17,900, 24,800 and 30,500 for add, mul and x²+y²). This is timing information, but no training-accuracy or delay is given.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its supports labels for V1 and V5 are not warranted. The only grokking 'results' are the criterion used to sort operations and the implicit status of the wd=0 controls. The study is by the same author as related spectral-edge preprints (Xu 2026a–c) and is not an original source. Neither row bears on a version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report when training accuracy saturates, whether test accuracy begins at chance, the delay between those events, or how delay changes with training-set size.

The study analyzes perturbation modes and spectral-edge dynamics, but does not measure gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or whether a continuous circuit-progress measure anticipates the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm/lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
Weight decay is compared, but the study does not test whether it favours a more efficient circuit over memorization, identify a critical dataset size, or test ungrokking below that size.
The study does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts as explanations of the delay.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer (single-task models; aggregate over the four grokking operations)
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular arithmetic with the stated weight-decay setting; report grokking/test-accuracy outcome.

conditions.value: (a + b), (a − b), (a · b), and (a² + b²) mod 97

rows.note: The report gives this outcome for the four operations as a group; it does not provide per-operation accuracy trajectories or training accuracy. This supports eventual high test accuracy, but not the claimed delay or its dependence on training-set size.
rows.check: This is a selection criterion, not a result. Section 2.1 uses '>95% test accuracy within 5000 steps' to define which operations count as grokking tasks. No training-accuracy saturation, delay or chance baseline is reported, so V1's delayed jump cannot be read from it. It is not a V5 measure.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer (single-task models; aggregate over the four operations designated as grokking tasks)
rows.operation_detail: Train on the same modular-arithmetic task group with weight decay set to zero; report grokking outcome.

conditions.value: (a + b), (a − b), (a · b), and (a² + b²) mod 97

rows.value: No grokking reported for the weight-decay-zero control conditions
rows.note: Reported as a control group, not as per-task accuracy values. The paper also describes the spectral edge as forming only under weight decay, but this row records the reported grokking outcome.
rows.check: No grokking outcome or accuracy is reported for the wd=0 runs. They appear only as 'Control (wd = 0, 4 ops)' in Table 1, and the study implies they are non-grokking. The value 'no grokking reported' is an inference from that labelling. Even taken at face value, weight-decay dependence of grokking does not test V5's efficiency mechanism, critical dataset size or ungrokking.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports test accuracy above 95% within 5000 steps for this task group (r1); it does not establish the claimed delay or training-set-size relationship.
